tagline: Up the Little Muskingum from Marietta, bridge by covered bridge.
intro: Out of Marietta, SR 26 swings around a hill, passes under I-77, crosses Duck Creek and winds into the hills, then takes up the Little Muskingum and keeps beside it most of the way through the Wayne National Forest. Ten marked stops interpret 35 miles of it, with four campgrounds along the way. In Monroe County the road leaves the river to climb through Graysville, meets it once more and ends in Woodsfield.
The river runs some 65 miles on a tight, meandering course, never more than 8 miles from the Ohio, and all but its last two miles lie inside the national forest.

moments.title: Dart
moments.text: Northeast of a hamlet said to be named for a bird flying past like a dart, the 1879 Hune Covered Bridge crosses the Little Muskingum on a Long truss, a style few bridges show.

moments.title: Wingett Run
moments.text: Just northeast, the Rinard Covered Bridge of 1876 was destroyed by a flash flood in September 2004 and rebuilt two years later.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Covered Bridge Scenic Byway
